articles.title: Want To Go To Law School? Get Ready For ‘Hyper Competition’ To Earn Your Seat
articles.content:
法学院入学竞争加剧：专家称面临"超高竞争"

《法学院入学竞争加剧：专家称面临"超高竞争"》
——编辑注：欢迎关注我们的每日专栏《每日引述》

"你将面临多年持续的显著增长，这意味着进入法学院的竞争将变得极其激烈。"
——迈克·斯派维（Mike Spivey），斯派维咨询公司（Spivey Consulting）的法学院入学咨询顾问，在接受路透社采访时就日益激烈的法学院入学竞争发表的评论。

今年申请法学院的人数同比增长了8%，去年则增长了18%。根据美国律师协会（ABA）认可的法学院入学咨询委员会（Law School Admission Council）的数据，今年有82,484人申请了美国律师协会认可的法学院，这是自金融危机以来申请人数最多的一年。

斯塔西·扎雷茨基（Staci Zaretsky）是《法律之上》（Above the Law）杂志的执行主编，自2011年起在该杂志工作。她非常欢迎读者的意见，如果您有任何建议、问题、评论或批评，请随时给她发邮件。您可以在Bluesky、X/Twitter和Threads上关注她，也可以在LinkedIn上与她联系。

（本文最初发表于《法律之上》杂志）
articles.summary:
Ed. note: Welcome to our daily feature, Quote of the Day.

You’re looking at a significant increase over multiple years. It means you have hyper competition to get into law school.

— Mike Spivey, law school admissions consultant with Spivey Consulting, in comments given to Reuters, concerning the increasingly competitive law school admissions landscape. The number of law school applicants rose 8% this year, following an 18% surge the year before. According to the Law School Admission Council, 82,484 people applied to ABA-accredited law schools this year, the largest applicant pool since the Great Recession.

Staci Zaretsky is the managing editor of Above the Law, where she’s worked since 2011. She’d love to hear from you, so please feel free to email her with any tips, questions, comments, or critiques. You can follow her on Bluesky, X/Twitter, and Threads, or connect with her on LinkedIn.

articles.title: FOIA Docs Show Brendan Carr Intimately Collaborated With White House, Right-Wing Propaganda Orgs
articles.content:
2014年，共和党曾长达两年时间对奥巴马政府的网络中立政策进行虚伪的指责。当时，共和党们试图让媒体相信，奥巴马政府公开支持联邦通信委员会（FCC）制定保护消费者和竞争的网络中立规则是违法的或施加过度压力的行为。哈德逊研究所等右翼智库更是大肆渲染这一"丑闻"，声称这"威胁到了我们的法治政府体系和互联网的发展"。

共和党国土安全和政府事务委员会甚至发起了一项持续两年的调查，最终发表了一份虚假报告，声称白宫与FCC之间存在诸多不当勾当。这里需要重复的是，共和党们当时对白宫就FCC正在推进的政策发表看法感到极度愤怒。

十二年后，网络中立政策早已名存实亡，这要归咎于共和党与电信垄断者之间的腐败勾结。如今，FCC实际上已成为白宫的附庸，任何关于FCC独立性的说法都变成了笑话。至少这是《卫报》根据信息自由法请求和公益组织"民主前进"提起的诉讼所公开的文件中透露的。

这些文件显示，FCC主席布伦丹·卡尔（Brendan Carr）与白宫和右翼宣传公司有着密切合作，推进了一系列政策，包括对新闻媒体的公然审查，以及（有时是非法的）削弱消费者保护、媒体合并限制和大部分公司监管措施等：

根据记录，2025年3月12日至2026年2月11日期间，卡尔至少八次在白宫参加会议，并至少与政府官员进行了三次约定的通话，包括与行政总监苏西·威尔斯（Susie Wiles）的两次对话。他还与政府官员如争议性卫生部长罗伯特·F·肯尼迪（Robert F Kennedy Jr.）通话。

此外，这些文件还揭示了卡尔的媒体策略，包括与福克斯新闻的制作人沟通，以及他与媒体巨头如福克斯公司首席执行官拉赫兰·默多克（Lachlan Murdoch）和辛克莱广播集团主席大卫·史密斯（David Smith）的秘密会面。

考虑到卡尔完全无视机构独立性的假象，与像福克斯新闻和辛克莱这样的右翼宣传工厂协调信息，并且不成比例地与右翼友好公司会面，为这些公司谋取私利，这一点不足为奇，也并非违法（在一个死气沉沉的腐败、游说和权钱交易法律环境下）。但这确实是共和党伪善的一个新高度。需要重复的是，十二年前，共和党（包括卡尔，他在担任FCC律师期间曾发言）坚称，总统就政策发表看法是非法的，是对FCC独立性的侵蚀。

需要明确的是，FCC应独立于白宫的影响，并受国会有效监督。但去年的国会听证会上，卡尔却引起争议，称该机构不再独立，甚至从机构网站上删除"独立"一词。

让监管机构成为独裁领导人任意操纵的木偶，显然是腐败和反民主的。如今，很难分清唐纳德·特朗普（Donald Trump）的任性想法从何处开始，FCC的所谓自主性又到何处结束，因为布伦丹·卡尔在骚扰对总统不利的媒体公司，并彻底剥离了美国剩余的消费者保护措施。

最终，卡尔可能得到的最严厉的处罚就是在AT&T资助的智库中获得一个高薪职位，然后在那里度过余生，用高额薪资继续破坏美国剩余的公共利益保障。
articles.summary:
Back in 2014 you might remember there was a giant, two-year, manufactured news cycle where Republicans pretended to be outraged that the then Obama White House had openly supported the FCC’s efforts to impose some modest net neutrality rules (designed to protect consumers and competition from telecom monopoly abuse of power).

At the time, major press outlets endlessly parroted Republican claims that the president’s perfectly legal public support of FCC policy was somehow underhanded, illegal, or applied undue pressure on an independent agency. Right wing friendly “think tanks” like the Hudson Institute suffered endless embolisms over the purported impropriety:

“The unwelcome assault on the independence of the FCC is a threat not merely to that agency. It is a threat to our entire system of government based on the rule of law. It is also a threat to the Internet. Where there is no rule of law, the Internet does not flourish.”

The Republican Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs even launched a two-year investigation culminating in a bogus report falsely claiming that there had been all sorts of nefarious intermingling between the White House and FCC. Republicans, I’ll repeat, were absolutely outraged that the White House would even open its mouth to comment on policy the agency was already pursuing.

Twelve years later and not only is net neutrality dead as a doornail thanks to corrupt collaboration between Republicans and telecom monopolies, but the FCC has taken up permanent residence inside the White House’s colon, making any claim of FCC independence laughable under Trumpism.

Or at least that’s the takeaway of this new report by the Guardian, which obtained documents via a Freedom of Information Act request and a lawsuit filed by the advocacy group Democracy Forward.

The documents show FCC boss Brendan Carr has had deep and intimate collaboration with both the White House and right wing propaganda companies as he’s pursued policies ranging from blatant censorship of of journalism and the media, to efforts to dismantle (at times illegally) consumer protections, media consolidation limits, and most corporate oversight:

“Between 12 March 2025 and 11 February 2026, Carr attended at least eight meetings at the White House, according to the records, and had at least three scheduled calls with administration officials, including two conversations with chief of staff Susie Wiles. He also spoke by phone with administration officials such as controversial health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr.

In addition, the files provide insight into Carr’s media strategy, including communications with producers at Fox News, and make public previously undisclosed meetings he has held with media titans such as Fox Corp chief executive Lachlan Murdoch and Sinclair Broadcast Group chair David Smith.”

That Carr is ignoring any pretense of agency independence, coordinating messaging with right wing agitprop factories like Fox News and Sinclair, and disproportionately meeting with right-wing friendly companies to their exclusive benefit shouldn’t surprise anybody and isn’t illegal (in a country with dead or dying corruption, lobbying, and influence-peddling laws), but it is a notable new high watermark for Republican hypocrisy. Twelve years ago, I’ll repeat, Republicans (including Carr, who had previously worked as an attorney at the agency), insisted the president even opening his mouth on policy was somehow illegal and an outrageous erosion of FCC independence.

The FCC is, to be clear, supposed to be independent from White House influence and meaningfully overseen by Congress. Though you might recall that last year in congressional testimony Carr raised eyebrows by insisting the agency is no longer independent — even going so far as to delete the word from the agency website.

Having regulators that are marionettes for the whims of your autocratic leadership is obviously corrupt and anti-democratic. Now it’s impossible to determine where Donald Trump’s incoherent whims begin and the FCC’s purported autonomy ends as Brendan Carr harasses media companies critical of the president, and strips away what’s left of U.S. consumer protection guardrails down to the studs.

Ultimately, I suspect the closest Carr will ever get to meaningful punishment is a revolving door gig at an AT&T-funded think tank where he whittles away the rest of his years getting paid high six figures to perpetuate the ongoing destruction of whatever’s left of U.S. public interest guardrails.

articles.title: An Open Letter To This Year’s Law Students
articles.content:
几天后，你们中的一些人将迈入法学院的第一堂课室。其他人则将回到大二或大三，带着更多的自信、更多的阅读量，以及大概更清楚咖啡馆的位置。

我羡慕你们。

不是因为我想念考试。
不是因为我想重温冷呼或期末考试的恐惧。
我羡慕你们，是因为你们正在开始你们的法律生涯，而这是我的一代从未有过的机会。

有趣的是，几乎没有人会在新生入学辅导时提到这一点。
你们会听到关于学习小组、实习、社交活动、期刊、诊所和暑期律师助理职位的介绍。你们会得到很多关于成绩和时间管理的好建议。

请听从所有这些建议。

但我想再补充一个建议。

开始写作。

不是为了成为博主。
不是为了吸引追随者。
因为写作会让你成为更好的律师。

我在读书时并没有明白这一点。
当时，我认为写作是律师在成为专家后才做的事情。你需要花几年时间学习、练习、积累信誉，之后才有值得分享的东西。

现在我认为我当时的想法是错误的。

你通过尝试解释你所学的内容，才会成为更好的律师。
第一次你坐下来尝试用简单的英语总结一个复杂的案件时，你会很快发现自己是否真正理解了它。
第一次你向一个从未读过法学院的人解释最高法院的判决时，你会意识到律师使用了多少不必要的专业术语。
第一次有人问你一个你无法回答的后续问题时，你会回去，更仔细地阅读，并比简单地在教材上划几行更好地记住这些内容。

写作有一种揭露你自己思维漏洞的方式。

这是一种礼物。

你们中有些人会立刻想到：“谁会想听一个一年级法学生的意见？”

这是一个错误的问题。

更好的问题是：
谁还在试图理解和你一样的事情？

总有一些学生正在为同一堂课做准备。
有一些大学生正在思考法学院是否适合他们。
有一些朋友想知道法院为什么做出了特定的决定。

你不需要假装自己是房间里最聪明的人。
你只需要诚实地分享你所学到的东西。

随着时间的推移，一些意想不到的事情会发生。

你不仅会成为更好的作家。
你会成为更清晰的思考者。
你会问出更好的问题。
你会更自如地解释复杂的想法，而不用依赖法律术语。

客户注意到了这一点。
法官注意到了这一点。
合伙人注意到了这一点。

在社交媒体出现之前，最好的律师几乎总是最好的沟通者。
这一点没有改变。

平台改变了。

还有一件事，我希望有人在读书时告诉我。

不要担心一开始几乎没有人阅读你的写作。
几乎没有人读过我的早期作品。
老实说，有些作品确实不值得被人阅读。

但这不是重点。

每一篇文章、每一篇帖子、每一次尝试解释一个想法都是练习。

不是为社交媒体练习。
而是为成为律师练习。

多年后，我意识到一件我从未想到的事。
人们不仅发现了我的内容。
他们还找到了我。

在他们联系我的办公室时，他们已经对我的思维方式、沟通方式和我关注的事情有了一定的了解。

我从未打算建立这样的影响力。

这发生了，是因为我一直在写作。

如果你们今秋开始法学院的学习，或者即将进入大二或大三，你们有一个机会，而这个机会在我坐在你们的位置时根本不存在。

你们可以用接下来的三年时间收集成绩和经历。
或者，你们可以用接下来的三年时间找到自己的声音。

一个会为你赢得学位。
另一个可能会塑造你的整个职业生涯。

如果我有机会重新开始，我会在第一周的课程中开始着手第二个。

阿曼达·德曼达是阿曼达·德曼达伤害律师事务所的创始人，是一位全国知名的审判律师，专注于严重和灾难性的商业卡车事故诉讼。她目前担任迈阿密-戴德试验律师协会主席。她建立了全国最具知名度的原告律师事务所之一，在迈阿密、坦帕、休斯顿、达拉斯以及佛罗里达州和德克萨斯州的其他地区设有办事处，使其团队能够处理关键交通枢纽中的高风险案件。阿曼达以融合法庭技巧和战略洞察力而闻名，她以人为本、以安全为导向的方法应对复杂的卡车和人身伤害案件，注重责任和现实影响。
articles.summary:
In a matter of days, some of you will walk into your very first law school class.

Others will head back for your second or third year, armed with a little more confidence, a lot more reading, and probably a better understanding of where the coffee is.

I envy you.

Not because I miss the exams.

Not because I’d love to relive cold calls or finals.

I envy you because you’re starting your legal career at a time when you have an opportunity my generation never had.

The funny thing is, almost nobody will mention it during orientation.

You’ll hear about study groups, internships, networking receptions, journals, clinics, and summer associate positions. You’ll get plenty of good advice about grades and time management.

Listen to all of it.

But I’d like to add one more suggestion.

Start writing.

Not because you’re trying to become an influencer.

Not because you’re trying to get followers.

Because writing will make you a better lawyer.

I didn’t understand that when I was in school.

Back then, I thought writing was something lawyers did after they had become experts. You spent years learning, years practicing, years earning credibility, and only then did you have something worth saying.

Now I think I had it backwards.

You become a better lawyer by trying to explain what you’re learning.

The first time you sit down and try to summarize a complicated case in plain English, you’ll discover very quickly whether you actually understood it.

The first time you explain a Supreme Court opinion to someone who has never been to law school, you’ll realize how much unnecessary jargon lawyers use.

The first time someone asks you a follow-up question you can’t answer, you’ll go back, read more carefully, and remember the material far better than if you’d simply highlighted another page in your casebook.

Writing has a way of exposing the gaps in your own thinking.

That’s a gift.

Some of you will immediately think, “Who wants to hear from a first-year law student?”

That’s the wrong question.

The better question is this:

Who else is trying to understand the same things you are?

There will always be another student preparing for the same class.

Another college student is wondering whether law school is right for them.

Another friend asked why a court reached a particular decision.

You don’t have to pretend to be the smartest person in the room.

You just have to be honest about what you’re learning.

Over time, something unexpected happens.

You don’t just become a better writer.

You become a clearer thinker.

You ask better questions.

You become more comfortable explaining complicated ideas without hiding behind legal terminology.

Clients notice that.

Judges notice that.

Partners notice that.

Long before social media, the best lawyers were almost always the best communicators.

That hasn’t changed.

The platforms have.

Here’s something else I wish someone had told me.

Don’t worry if hardly anyone reads what you write at first.

Almost nobody read my early work.

Honestly, some of it deserved that fate.

But that’s not the point.

Every article, every post, every attempt to explain an idea was practice.

Not practice for social media.

Practice for being a lawyer.

Years later, I realized something I never expected.

People weren’t just finding my content.

They were finding me.

By the time some of them called my office, they already had a sense of how I thought, how I communicated, and what mattered to me.

I never set out to build that.

It happened because I kept writing.

If you’re beginning law school this fall—or heading into your second or third year—you have an opportunity that simply didn’t exist when I was sitting where you are.

You can spend the next three years collecting grades and experiences.

Or you can spend the next three years finding your voice.

One earns you a degree.

The other can shape your entire career.

If I had the chance to start over again, I know exactly which one I’d begin working on the first week of classes

Amanda Demanda is the founder of Amanda Demanda Injury Lawyers and a nationally recognized trial attorney with a focus on serious and catastrophic commercial truck accident litigation. She currently serves as President of the Miami-Dade Trial Lawyers Association. She has built one of the most visible plaintiff firms in the country, with offices in Miami, Tampa, Houston, Dallas, and throughout Florida and Texas, allowing her team to handle high-stakes cases across key transportation corridors. Known for blending courtroom skill with strategic insight, Amanda brings a people-first, safety-driven approach to complex trucking and personal injury cases, with a focus on accountability and real-world impact.

The post An Open Letter To This Year’s Law Students appeared first on Above the Law.

articles.title: Former Federal Prosecutor Indicted For Allegedly Threatening To Murder Old Bosses — And Their Kids
articles.content:
纳什维尔联邦大陪审团于8月19日对前联邦助理检察官亚历山大·施特罗梅耶起诉。7月30日提交并密封的刑事起诉书于本周四解封，指控这位前联邦检察官威胁要谋杀他在检察官办公室的前上司，并威胁他们的孩子。当事人通过屏幕截图提供了相关证据。

今天的法院观察通讯中，西摩·休斯和彼得·贝克特将此案列为重点案件。施特罗梅耶于2024年8月8日左右被联邦检察官办公室解雇，此前他在一般犯罪和白领犯罪部门工作了一年，期间处理了暴力犯罪、枪支和毒品案件。根据他目前在贝格·希尔·格林利夫·鲁斯基蒂律师事务所的个人简介，他曾负责处理暴力犯罪、枪支和毒品案件。2026年7月22日，威廉姆森县警长办公室根据田纳西州的亲密数字描述法典获取了对他的逮捕令。第二天，大法官服务机构接管了这份逮捕令，开始了对他的通缉调查，并于8月3日在科罗拉多州将其逮捕，当时他正在博尔德的公司从事复杂的商业诉讼。

而所谓的“亲密数字描述”指的是：
施特罗梅耶将受害者的比基尼照片提交给了一个人工智能平台，并创建了一个视频和/或图像，描绘受害者的裸体身体，而未经她的同意。施特罗梅耶在电子通信中告诉受害者，他拥有该视频和/或图像，并且将通过发送它来使用视频和/或图像，从而破坏受害者的名誉。

“如果我只是和黑社会有联系，或者能够不留痕迹地行动就好了。”起诉书中包含的聊天记录如是说。伙计，你甚至不需要联系黑社会，只需要遵循斯特林格·贝尔的建议，不要留下任何书面记录的犯罪证据。

不幸的是，这并不是该案涉及的所有违法行为：
在州一级的案件中，施特罗梅耶被控在一段时间内向受害者发送多条威胁性短信息。其中，电子通信告诉受害者，她的孩子“并非安全无虞”。受害者将此理解为她的孩子的生命受到威胁。此外，施特罗梅耶表示，他可以通过“按下一个按钮”或“改装的AR-15扳机”来毁掉受害者的生活。

起诉书中包含的聊天记录还描述了更多的威胁。

祝贺OpenAI，他们可以将此案加入其宣传守则的幻灯片中。

该案中提到的短信内容——谈论犯罪集团、AR-15步枪和毒害儿童——确实令人毛骨悚然。另一方面，他并没有发送任何随机贝壳的照片，所以谁也无法确定这是否是真正的威胁。

articles.summary:
A federal grand jury in Nashville indicted a former Assistant U.S. Attorney on August 19. The underlying criminal complaint — filed under seal on July 30 and unsealed Thursday claims former federal prosecutor Alexander Strohmeyer threatened to murder his former bosses at the office and made threats against their kids. And there are screenshots.

Seamus Hughes & Peter Beck flagged this case in today’s Court Watch round up. Strohmeyer was terminated from the U.S. Attorney’s Office on or about August 8, 2024, after about a year in the General Crimes and White Collar units, where, per his current Berg Hill Greenleaf Ruscitti LLP bio, he handled violent crime, firearms, and narcotics cases. On July 22, 2026, the Williamson County Sheriff’s Office obtained a warrant charging him under Tennessee’s intimate digital depictions statute. The Marshals Service adopted the warrant the next day, opened a fugitive investigation, and arrested him in Colorado on August 3, where he had landed at the Boulder firm doing complex commercial litigation.

And by intimate digital descriptions, we mean…

STROHMEYER submitted photos of the victim in a bikini to an Artificial Intelligence platform and created a video and/or images depicting the victim’s nude body without her consent. STROHMEYER stated via electronic communications to the victim that he had said video and/or images and that he would use the video and/or images by sending it out and destroying the victim’s reputation.

“If only I were like connected to the underworld or something and could operate untraced,” a chat log included in the complaint states. Bro, you don’t even need to be connected to take Stringer Bell’s advice and not create a written record of criminal activity.

Unfortunately, this wasn’t the extent of the alleged wrongdoing:

In summary, STROHMEYER is accused in the state case of sending the victim multiple and threatening text messages over a period of time. Among other things, the electronic communications stated to the victim her children “were not off the table.” The victim took this to
mean the lives of her children were being threatened. Additionally, STROHMEYER stated he could ruin the victim’s life with “the press of a button or a modded AR-15 trigger.”

The chat log included in the complaint outline even more threats.

Congratulations to OpenAI, who can add this to the slide deck touting its guardrails.

The texts identified in this case — talking about criminal gangs, AR-15s, and poisoning children — seem genuinely disturbing. On the other hand, he did not send a picture of some random seashells, so who can really say if this is a real threat?

#187: The Justice Department Owns a Bar [Court Watch]

Joe Patrice is a senior editor at Above the Law and co-host of Thinking Like A Lawyer. Feel free to email any tips, questions, or comments. Follow him on Twitter or Bluesky if you’re interested in law, politics, and a healthy dose of college sports news.

articles.title: ILTACON 2026: Separating Wheat From Chaff
articles.content:
2026年国际法律技术协会（ILTA）举办的大型法律科技展览会将于8月24日在纳什维尔的盖洛德酒店和会议中心拉开帷幕，为期四天，内容包括教育研讨会、网络交流活动和产品宣传推广。

正如Irvin S. Cobb所言：除非你亲自参加ILTACON并亲眼目睹，否则你真的什么都没见过—至少在法律科技领域是这样。然而，在这类大型知名活动中，如何分清真正有价值的内容和商业噱头，始终是一项挑战。作为一名从事法律科技报道的资深记者，我已连续多年参加ILTACON，希望这次能做到这一点。

**ILTA与会议**
ILTA自称是一个全球性的志愿者组织，致力于推动法律领域有效应用技术的同行学习与分享。本届大会将提供超过80场教育研讨会，并设有庞大的展览厅。ILTA将其称为“法律领域首屈一指的教育与网络交流活动”。从规模上看，ILTACON确实是法律科技会议中数一数二的，预计今年的参会人数将接近甚至超过去年的创纪录水平。

虽然活动通常组织得井井有条，但有时也会像超级碗半场表演一样缺乏细腻感，容易沦为大型律所技术采购经理的商业推销舞台。

**ILTACON内容**
今年的宣传活动似乎较往年低调，没有发现过往年那样的标语口号或情感化宣传视频，而是更加注重内容本身。ILTA表示，内容设计“满足多样化的学习需求，包括学习路径、专家讨论、实践培训和参会者主导的研讨会”。

公布的教育研讨会内容包括：
- AI治理与跨平台集成专题；
- IT部门如何更具战略性地部署AI和自动化；
- 现代法律实务中如何更好地利用自动化技术；
- 尤其引人关注的是，当技术提升律师效率时，如何应对“以时间计费”的商业模式带来的矛盾。

这些议题看起来都颇具吸引力和相关性，但具体效果还需现场验证。

**主题演讲**
大会设置了两场主题演讲（不包括NetDocuments CEO Dan Hauck主持的律所CIO圆桌讨论）。Hauck主持的圆桌讨论可能会成为三场演讲中最有启发性的环节。

今年的两位主题演讲者分别是：
- 曾效力于美国职业棒球大联盟的Jim Abbott，尽管天生右手残疾但仍取得成功，现为知名演讲家和作家；
- 曾任NASA医生的Dr. Kevin Fong，医生、广播员和作家。

ILTA选择了与法律和技术领域关联不大的激励型名人演讲者，这种做法可能会有两种结果。如果演讲者充分了解听众，并将个人故事与法律行业结合起来，效果可能不错；否则可能无法与法律专业内容建立联系，浪费时间。

Abbott和Fong的演讲值得期待，但作为经常参加会议的观察者，我对这类“克服人生困难”的激励演讲已经略有疲劳。

**9/11纪念**
值得一提的是，ILTA计划在会议期间举办9/11纪念活动，包括设立纪念墙、播放视频回顾等，并展示法律科技社区成员在袭击事件中的亲身经历和故事。这个设计很有意义，随着时间推移，我们容易忽视那场事件带来的国家创伤。记得当时我正在处理一起重大火灾诉讼案，雇佣了一位曾与纽约消防局合作的专家，他告诉我，9/11之后的几个月，他几乎每天都在参加认识或合作过的人的葬礼。

**静心空间**
今年新增的一个亮点是显著扩大的静心放松空间，为参会者提供休憩之所。这个空间不仅提供休息场所，还将配备心理健康资源、保健建议、食谱和饮品等。ILTA还将提供电解质补充剂、蛋白饮料、特调咖啡等。

在参会者紧张的日程中，这个空间可能是一个难得的休整之地。在会议期间，参会者需要步行数英里，连续参加研讨会，晚上则是各种网络交流活动，往往需要在拥挤的酒吧里大声讨论AI等话题。

**参会人群**
ILTA主要面向大律所，参会者通常是CIO、COO、IT人员、创新官、法律运营专家以及针对这些人群的服务商。然而，很少有在职律师参加ILTACON或其他法律科技会议（除了ABA TechShow）。

这种情况导致会议内容主要围绕向技术采购决策影响者推销产品展开，而非展示律师如何在日常工作中使用这些产品及其实际效益。实则，销售对象通常并非律所最终决策者，而是需要将技术信息传达给缺乏相关知识的律师。结果往往是采购的产品无法解决实际问题，或达不到预期效果。

无论如何，本届会议将有众多产品发布和AI技术的宣传，各大供应商将争相展示其产品的独特AI功能，并举办多场产品演示和推销活动。巨大的展览厅内将充斥着各种销售人员。

**总结**
ILTACON是一场为期四天的教育研讨会、产品推销、网络交流和社交活动的盛会。会议举办在盖洛德酒店和会议中心—一个大到需要专门应用才能帮助参会者导航的场所。

作为全程参与的记者，我将实时报道会议动态。这场会议总是充满各种活动，值得关注的亮点不断，当然也少不了各种社交活动（当然，我指的是网络交流活动）。我将努力挖掘信息，让大家了解法律科技市场的真实情况。当然，最终我会带着疲惫归来。

（Stephen Embry是律师、演讲者、博主和作家，主持TechLaw Crossroads博客，专注探讨技术、法律与法律实务之间的张力。）

（原文首发于Above the Law网站）
articles.summary:
The 2026 giant legal tech show put on by the International Legal Technology Association (ILTA) kicks off August 24th at the Gaylord Hotel and Convention Center in Nashville. It is four nonstop days of educational sessions, networking events, and sales pitches. 

Indeed, to paraphrase Irvin S. Cobb: Until you go to ILTACON and behold it with your own eyes, you ain’t never been nowhere and you ain’t seen nothing. At least not in legal tech.

But with anything this big and this well known, separating the wheat from the sales chaff is always a challenge. I’ve been to ILTACON almost every year since leaving the full-time practice of law to be a legal tech journalist, so I hope I’m up to it.

ILTA and The Conference

ILTA describes itself as a global organization led by volunteers, which promotes peer-to-peer learning and sharing about the effective use of technology in law.

In keeping with that mission, this year’s conference will feature over 80 educational sessions and undoubtedly a rocking exhibit hall. ILTA itself labels the conference “as the premier educational and networking event for the legal sector.” 

And well, it could be. It is certainly one of the biggest, if not the biggest, of the legal tech conferences. And I suspect it will come close to surpassing last year’s record-setting attendance.

And while the show is usually well planned and well executed, as noted before, it sometimes has the subtlety of a Super Bowl halftime show. It can be one big, gigantic sales pitch by vendors marketing to those in large law firms they think have money to burn.

ILTACON Content

This year, however, the pre-show hype at least seems to be a bit toned down. There are no catchy, cutesy promotional themes or schmaltzy videos as in years past, at least that I could find. Instead, ILTA seems to be more focused on content.

And according to ILTA, the content is designed “to meet a variety of learning styles that include learning pathways, panel discussions, hands-on training, and attendee-driven sessions.”

The content substance is pretty much what you might expect. The education sessions highlighted by ILTA in its recent newsletter include:

• A session on AI governance, particularly with respect to integration with various platforms, 

• A discussion on how IT departments can better and more strategically deploy AI and automation, 

• A session directed at how to better use modern practice practical strategies for using automation, and, 

• Perhaps most interestingly, a discussion of that uncomfortable little issue of what happens when tech makes lawyers more efficient inside a business model that makes money when lawyers take longer to do something, not shorter.

All of these sound interesting and relevant, at least on paper. I’ll let you know. 

The Keynotes

There are also two keynotes. Well, three, if you count the roundtable discussion with CIOs from various large law firms, led by Dan Hauck, the CEO of NetDocuments. Knowing Hauck, that session may well prove to be the most enlightening of the three.

With respect to the other two keynotes, like many organizations putting on legal tech shows these days, ILTA has elected to go with motivational, celebrity speakers who have little obvious connection to either law or technology.

As I have discussed before, that can go one of two ways. If the speakers understand the audience, do the homework, and make the connection between their personal story and the profession, it can go well. If not, and if they aren’t well prepared to relate their discussion to legal, it can be a waste of time. 

One of the two keynoters this year is Jim Abbott. Abbott is a former Major League Baseball player who was quite successful despite being born without a right hand. He is a well-known speaker and writer. One thing he is definitely not is a lawyer, legal professional, or technologist. 

The other keynote speaker is Dr. Kevin Fong, a doctor, broadcaster, and former NASA physician. Fong spoke at ILTA’s Evolve Conference back in the spring where he basically told a series of what appeared to me to be disjointed stories with little legal connection. The folks at ILTA must have liked him, however, since he’s back so soon.

But keep in mind, I go to a lot of conferences and have heard more or less the same motivational speech from those who all have overcome something in their lives. To say I’m a bit jaded may be an understatement.

A 9/11 Tribute

On a serious note, ILTA reportedly plans to commemorate 9/11 at the conference, including holding a memorial, a wall of remembrance, and a video presentation during the Fong Keynote. It will highlight members of the legal technology community who actually experienced the attacks, their aftermath, and their stories.

Nice touch, ILTA. As years go by, we often forget that day and the national trauma. It impacted all of us one way or the other. I was engaged in significant fire litigation at the time and engaged an expert at one time associated with NYFD. He told me that for months after 9/11, all he did was go to funerals of people he knew and worked with. It was a sad time.

Tranquility Base

It’s also worth mentioning one semi-new addition this year: there is a significantly amped up wellness and tranquility space for some peace and quiet.

But it’s not just a room to sit and ponder. It will reportedly also have a number of mindfulness resources, take-home wellness tips, recipes, and ideas for beverages and wellness activities. ILTA is also offering things like electrolyte shots, protein drinks, specialty coffee, etc. 

Whether this is a real effort to offer some real mental and physical wellness options remains to be seen. But it’s a nice idea, especially considering how hectic the conference can be. You walk miles. You have constant meetings. You go to session after session. Then you spend the evening networking, which often involves standing at a crowded bar shouting about AI.

So given my schedule of meetings, networking, and educational sessions, I may need to spend some time in the wellness room. If only I can find the time.

The ILTACON Audience

As I have noted before, ILTA is primarily for Biglaw. The attendees are typically CIOs, COOs, IT personnel, innovation officers, legal operations professionals, and the vendors who market and sell to these folks.

But as I have griped before, there are very few practicing lawyers who attend ILTA, or, for that matter, any other legal tech conference, perhaps save ABA TechShow.

Given that, much of what happens at ILTACON is directed at and focused on selling products to the people the vendors think can somehow influence law firms’ purchases. The pitches are less designed to show how lawyers and legal professionals — you know, the ones who actually use the stuff — might work with the products on a day-to-day level and what benefits come from them. 

And the reality is that the pitches are in fact being made not to the final decision-makers in most firms but to those who report to the final decision-makers. As a result, the pitches have to be repeated by those with technical knowledge who have heard them to lawyers who don’t have the same level of technical expertise. The all too often result: the purchase of products that don’t address a pain point and don’t work as expected.  

In any event, there will most assuredly be a bunch of product announcements by vendors breathlessly declaring that some product you vaguely remember from before now contains AI. People explaining why their AI is different than anyone else’s. Lots of meetings hosted by the vendors, plenty of demonstrations designed to sell the products, and a vast exhibit floor chock full of sales personnel.

The Not-So Bottom Line

The more or less bottom line is ILTACON is four days of nonstop educational sessions, sales pitches, networking, and partying. Perhaps apropos of the nature of the conference, it’s being held at the cavernous Gaylord Hotel and Convention Center. A convention center so big, by the way, that when you check in, Gaylord offers you an app to help you find your way around. That should tell you all you need to know about the Gaylord and the size of ILTACON.

I will be there for the duration to report what I see and experience. It’s always crazy with lots going on, lots to see and, of course, lots of parties (oops, I mean… networking events). I will certainly try to dig out from under all the hype to see what is really being offered, discussed, and pitched. That will tell us something about the state of the legal technology market. 

And, of course, as always, I will come home exhausted.  

Stephen Embry is a lawyer, speaker, blogger, and writer. He publishes TechLaw Crossroads, a blog devoted to the examination of the tension between technology, the law, and the practice of law.
